name: The Mirror Blinked
blurb: Brushing teeth at 1 a.m., someone notices their reflection is half a second behind
title: The Mirror Blinked: 45-Second Horror Short Script for 1
description: A 45-second vertical micro horror script for 1 actor: at 1 a.m. a reflection falls half a second out of sync. Creepy, not graphic, free to film.
h1: The Mirror Blinked: a 45-Second Horror Short Script for 1 Actor
logline: Getting ready for bed at 1 a.m., someone notices their reflection stops brushing half a second late. They test it, laugh it off, and test it again. Then they switch off the light, and the mirror is not finished.
setting: A small bathroom at night with one light. Props: a toothbrush, a towel, a mirror, a phone on a tripod.

roles.name: Robin
roles.note: Teen to adult, any gender, exhausted, rational, trying hard not to be scared; also plays the reflection.

script.action: ROBIN, half asleep, brushes their teeth at the mirror. One warm light.
Robin stops brushing. In the mirror, the brush stops half a second later.
Robin rinses, wipes their face, looks up. Slowly raises one hand.
The reflection raises its hand. Late.
Robin leans close. Blinks twice, hard.
Robin backs away and switches off the light.
Robin stops in the doorway, back to the mirror.
A beat. From the dark mirror, in Robin's voice:

script.sfx: Click. The light comes back on.

script.action: In the mirror, the reflection stands where Robin was, hand on the switch, smiling. Cut to black.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 on a tripod, never handheld, because the trick needs a locked frame. Film the mirror at an angle so the camera does not appear in it. For the late reflection, shoot the same action twice and in the edit mask the mirror area with the second, delayed take; for a no-edit version, use a doorway or an empty frame as the mirror and have the actor's reflection played on the other side by the same actor in a second take. Use one warm light only and a phone torch for the dark shots. Record the whisper separately, close to the phone, and keep it very quiet.

ul: Robin is tired, not scared, at first. Yawning and slow movements make the first glitch easy to miss, which is creepier.
Each test should be smaller and more careful than the last. Fear shows in stillness, not screaming.
The reflection never overacts. A delay of half a second and a tiny, calm smile are enough.
After stop it, hold the silence. Let the viewer listen to the room before the light goes off.
The last shot must be short. Show the smile for about a second, then cut to black so the sting lands.
Set it in a lift with a mirrored wall, a car's rear-view mirror or a dark phone screen that reflects a face a beat late.
Add a second actor as a flatmate who knocks on the door at the end, and the reflection answers instead of Robin.
Part-two hook: the next morning Robin waves at the mirror, and the reflection waves first.

prompts.keyframe: Tired young adult brushing teeth in a small bathroom at night, seen over the shoulder in the mirror, single warm bulb, dark doorway behind, quiet uneasy atmosphere, cinematic still, vertical 9:16.
shots: Vertical 9:16 locked-off shot of a bathroom mirror, a young adult stops brushing their teeth but the reflection keeps moving for half a second, single warm light, subtle eerie mood.
Close-up of a young adult leaning toward a mirror and blinking, the reflection blinks out of time, shallow depth of field, dim warm light, growing dread.
Wide shot from a dark doorway, a young adult switches off the bathroom light and stands still with their back to the mirror, almost total darkness, tense quiet mood.
Static shot on a bathroom mirror as the light flicks back on, the reflection stands alone with a hand on the switch and a calm smile, then cut to black, creepy sting.

faq.q: How do I make the reflection out of sync with only a phone?
faq.a: Lock the phone on a tripod and shoot each action twice. In any free editing app, crop the second take to the mirror area, lay it over the first and shift it half a second later.

faq.q: Is this scary enough for a horror channel but safe for school?
faq.a: Yes. Nothing violent happens and there is no blood; the fear comes from timing and silence. It is suitable for school film projects and every platform.

faq.q: Can I use it on a monetised horror channel?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0, including monetised channels and competitions. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the description.
